name: Littlestone Dimension / Log Size Ratio
details: For every finite binary class, Littlestone dimension is at least its Log Size Ratio.
proof: On an $n$-point domain, use the complete depth-$n$ tree that queries the coordinates in one fixed order on every level. Its zero-cover has one distinct leaf labeling for each member of $\mathcal H$, hence size $|\mathcal H|$. Rakhlin--Sridharan--Tewari's sequential Sauer bound gives $|\mathcal H|\leq\sum_{i=0}^L\binom ni\leq(n+1)^L$ for $L=\mathrm{Ldim}(\mathcal H)$. Therefore $L\geq\log(|\mathcal H|-1)/\log(n+1)=\mathrm{LSR}(\mathcal H)$, with the singleton convention handled separately.
